text:
Alex C.: Quick q — I'm starting Mon 3/14 and my offer included a relocation signing bonus + a commuter stipend. A few questions: 1) Is the signing bonus taxed on my first paycheck or as a separate bonus? 2) When does the commuter stipend card activate (my start week overlaps a company holiday)? 3) Domestic partner enrollment — do I need proof of partnership or is a signed affidavit enough? Thanks!

Sophie (People Ops): Congrats and welcome, Alex! Short answers: 1) Usually the signing bonus is processed as a separate taxable bonus on the first payroll after onboarding. 2) Commuter card ships within ~5 business days and activates after we mark you active — if your start week has a company holiday there can be a small delay. 3) DP affidavit + one supporting doc (utility bill or joint lease) is standard. I'll DM a checklist and the portal link. :tada:

Raj (Payroll): +1 to Sophie. We treat signing bonuses as supplemental income, taxed per applicable federal/state rules. On our side it shows up as a line item "Signing Bonus" and is usually included on the next payroll run after your paperwork clears. If you need the bonus timing/split to match cashflow, reply here and we can check the offer terms. Also confirm your payroll state/timezone.

Alex C.: Thanks — what's the ETA for "next payroll run"? first paycheck timing is a bit tight for me.

Raj (Payroll): If onboarding paperwork (I-9, W-4, direct deposit) is completed by 3/20 we can include you in the 3/31 run (paid 4/7). If not, it'll be the subsequent run. I can follow up via DM with exact dates for CA employees.

Lena (Benefits): For DP coverage, enroll in the benefits portal within 30 days of your start date. We need the signed affidavit + one supporting doc dated within the last 60 days (utility, bank statement, lease). If your partner has other primary coverage, we'll request COB forms. If you want we can fast-track verification once you upload docs.

Alex C.: I uploaded the signed DP affidavit to the portal but the status still says "pending verification". Anything else I should do?

Sophie (People Ops): I can see the upload — thanks. We still need a supporting doc (utility or joint bank) to complete verification. If you don't have a joint doc yet, a declaration plus an alternate doc (e.g., shared lease) works. I'll DM the exact accepted file types.

Raj (Payroll): Also heads-up: commuter stipend may be taxable depending on state. If you're in CA it will likely be subject to state withholding. Once you DM me your payroll state I'll run the tax treatment for the stipend + bonus so you know net amounts.

hr-bot: Reminder: New hire benefits enrollments close 30 days from start. Required documents for DP enrollment: signed DP affidavit, supporting doc, completed W-4, direct deposit set up.

Alex C.: Perfect — I'll DM Sophie the utility PDF and ping Raj my CA details. Appreciate the quick help! :thumbsup:
